title: DR1 lets a trader attach fifteen documents and says so up front; the frontend stops at ten and only mentions a limit once the eleventh is refused.

finding.frontend: The documents collection is capped at ten entries (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:19-28). An eleventh attempt is refused before any validation runs, with the summary error "You can add a maximum of 10 documents" pointing at the added-documents table (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:92-100). Nothing on the page warns of the cap beforehand: the file requirements hint lists only a size and a set of file types (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:43-49). No captured frontend state shows the refusal — both frontend captures hold zero or one document.
finding.prototype: DR1's ceiling is fifteen and the trader is told before they start: "up to a maximum of 15 files" is the third bullet in the file requirements list. Reaching it is captured at dr1-upload-documents-limit-error — fifteen rows in the table and a single error, "You can upload a maximum of 15 files", shown both in the summary and against the Attachment field, with the rest of the form's validation skipped (app/views/upload-documents.html:165-170).
finding.difference: Raise maxEntries from 10 to 15, restate the error as "You can upload a maximum of 15 files", and add the ceiling to the file requirements bullets so the trader meets it before they hit it. Attaching the error to the Attachment field rather than to the table, as DR1 does, is part of the same change. Nothing outside the frontend holds a competing cap, so the three edits are the whole of the work.
finding.falsifiedBy: Adding an eleventh document through the frontend and having it saved.
finding.verification: Read both sides. The frontend cap is maxEntries: 10 at obligations/sections/documents.js:25 inside the cited 19-28, and the refusal at controller.js:96-100 does precede documentAddErrors at :101, so "refused before any validation runs" is exact; the message is built as `You can add a maximum of ${max} documents` (copy.en.js:73) and anchored to the added-documents table (form/errors.js:52-56), and neither frontend capture's hint mentions a count. DR1's side is captured rather than inferred: dr1-upload-documents-limit-error holds fifteen table rows and exactly one error, "You can upload a maximum of 15 files", linked to #attachment, with no other field in error — confirming the early return that skips the rest of validation at routes.js:9106-9113, and "up to a maximum of 15 files" is the third requirements bullet in the DOM. Every quoted string matches character for character. CORRECT on the claim; one supporting sentence fell, see correction.
finding.correction: The difference slot asked the reader to "Check the backend's own accompanying-document cap before raising the frontend one", on the reasoning that the error code obligation.accompanyingDocument.tooMany "implies a matching rule on the far side". It does not. That string occurs in exactly two places in the frontend and nowhere else: the obligation itself (obligations/sections/documents.js:26, declared on the same object as maxEntries: 10) and an obligation-evaluator test. A search of trade-imports-animals-backend src/main returns no occurrence of the code, of tooMany, or of any accompanying-document count limit at all. The code names the frontend's own obligation-model failure, not a backend contract. The sentence has been struck and replaced; the band was already frontend-work and is now unqualified rather than hedged.

relatedTo.why: both rewrite the same four-line file requirements list
